land.text: Jaffna peninsula and Kilinochchi, the land the Tigers took after the IPKF left in 1989-90

predecessors.note: The LTTE itself was founded on 5 May 1976 (LTTE page) and fought from 23 July 1983; it held a de facto state from about 1990.

successors.note: The whole rebel zone returned to the government between July 2007 and 18 May 2009.

capitals.name: Kilinochchi
capitals.note: LTTE page: the de facto state 'named Tamil Eelam with Kilinochchi as its administrative capital'; troops took 'Kilinochchi, the city which the LTTE had used for over a decade as its de facto administrative capital' on 2 January 2009. The government held the town from 29 September 1996 to 27 September 1998; no page names a seat before that.

correction.text: Jaffna peninsula and the Kilinochchi district: 'the key rebel stronghold of Jaffna' (1995) and the Vanni seat

keyframe_review.note: Jaffna held by the Tigers until 5 December 1995 (Operation Riviresa); the army's 1990 and February 1992 offensives 'failed to capture Jaffna'. District-level reading; no page gives the extent.

correction.text: Mullaitivu (overrun 18 July 1996) and the Kilinochchi district outside the town the army held from 29 September 1996 to 27 September 1998

keyframe_review.note: Jaffna lost in December 1995. Kilinochchi town is carried by the ledger events of 1996 and 1998.

correction.text: the Vanni: 'Nearly all the Vanni rapidly fell back into LTTE hands'

keyframe_review.note: Vavuniya is named on no page and left out. The A9 highway later 'ran through LTTE territory' (2002).

correction.text: the Vanni and the Eastern Province: 'at its peak in 2000, the LTTE was in control of 76% of the landmass in the Northern and Eastern provinces'

keyframe_review.note: Whole districts overstate it: the government kept the towns of Vavuniya and Trincomalee and the Jaffna peninsula's core, and the Tigers held about three quarters of the two provinces (the Tamil Eelam page's claimed area is 18,880 km2 of which 17,651 km2 land). The east was bridged at confidence 1.

correction.text: the Vanni after the loss of the east: 11 July 2007, 'ending the LTTE's military capability in the Eastern Province'

keyframe_review.note: Mannar District was lost by 2 August 2008 (ledger). A 140 km2 jungle pocket at Thoppigala survived the July 2007 fall.

correction.text: what remained after Kilinochchi (2 January 2009) and Mullaitivu town (25 January 2009)

keyframe_review.note: The last pocket was captured on 18 May 2009 (Tamil Eelam page).

region.text: Jaffna peninsula and the Kilinochchi district

ledger.note: 1990: the Tigers set up their de facto state. 'When the Indian Peace-Keeping Force withdrew in 1989-90, the LTTE established many government-like functions in the areas under its control' and 'swiftly took control of a significant portion of the territory'; the Tamil Eelam page has it 'under de facto control of the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) for most of the 1990s-2000s'. No page gives the year or the land: 1990 is the IPKF's departure (last ship 24 March 1990) and the land is the researcher's reading.

5 December 1995: the army retakes Jaffna. Operation Riviresa brought 'Jaffna under government control for the first time in nearly a decade'; the national flag was raised 'inside the Jaffna Fort on 5 December 1995'. Over 350,000 civilians fled to the Vanni.

region.text: the Mullaitivu district around the town where the army base fell

ledger.note: 18 July 1996: the Tigers overrun Mullaitivu. The LTTE 'decisively won the Battle of Mullaitivu on 18 July 1996, leaving 1,173 army troops dead'. The page gives the battle, not a district; the district is the researcher's reading.

29 September 1996: Kilinochchi taken. 'The town of Kilinochchi was taken on 29 September', after 'The government launched another offensive in August 1996'; the sentence does not name the force. The district outside the town stayed LTTE ground.
27 September 1998: the Tigers retake Kilinochchi. 'On 27 September 1998 the LTTE launched Operation Unceasing Waves II and, after heavy fighting, captured Kilinochchi.'

region.text: the Vanni: Mannar, Kilinochchi and Mullaitivu

ledger.note: 1999: the Vanni goes back to the Tigers. 'Nearly all the Vanni rapidly fell back into LTTE hands.' The page names the Vanni, not the districts; Mannar, Kilinochchi and Mullaitivu are the researcher's reading, and Vavuniya, named on no page, is left out. Month: the Sri Lankan civil war page places it in 'Operation Unceasing Waves III on 2 November 1999' (added by reviewer sa-06-e, 2026-10-25).

region.text: the Eastern Province: Batticaloa, Trincomalee and Ampara districts

ledger.note: 2000: the Tigers' peak. 'at its peak in 2000, the LTTE was in control of 76% of the landmass in the Northern and Eastern provinces'. Page silent on when the east came under the Tigers or which districts; the Eastern Province is bridged here from the 2007 recapture, so the reviewer should treat this as a gap. Vavuniya and Trincomalee town are named nowhere.

region.text: the Elephant Pass military complex between the Jaffna peninsula and the Vanni

ledger.note: 22 April 2000: Elephant Pass falls. 'On 22 April 2000 the Elephant Pass military complex, which had separated the Jaffna peninsula from the Vanni mainland for 17 years, fell into the hands of the LTTE'; 'After securing a vast area formerly controlled by the military, the LTTE further advanced northwards' (2001).

region.text: the Eastern Province: Batticaloa, Trincomalee and Ampara districts

ledger.note: 11 July 2007: the army takes Thoppigala and the east. 'the army captured the Thoppigala peak on 11 July 2007, ending the LTTE's military capability in the Eastern Province'; the Tigers kept 'a 140-square-kilometre pocket of jungle in the Thoppigala area'.
By 2 August 2008: Mannar District is lost by the Tigers. 'By 2 August 2008, LTTE lost the Mannar District following the fall of Vellankulam town.'

region.text: the Kilinochchi district, the Tigers' administrative capital

ledger.note: 2 January 2009: Kilinochchi captured. Troops took 'Kilinochchi, the city which the LTTE had used for over a decade as its de facto administrative capital.' The page names the city; the district is the researcher's reading.

region.text: the Mullaitivu district around the town

ledger.note: 25 January 2009: Mullaitivu town captured. On 25 January 2009 troops 'completely captured' Mullaitivu town.

18 May 2009: the Tamil Eelam de facto state ends. 'The last pocket of territory controlled by the LTTE was captured by the Sri Lankan Army on 18 May 2009'; 'Since 19 May 2009 Tamil Eelam has ceased to exist as a physical entity but remains as political aspiration.'

wars.name: Sri Lankan Civil War

zones.text: the Northern and Eastern provinces: the eight districts of the claimed Tamil Eelam

wars.outcome: The Tigers held a de facto state in the north and east from about 1990 until their defeat on 18 May 2009.
wars.note: Eelam War I from 23 July 1983; Eelam War II after the IPKF left (1990); Eelam War III from 19 April 1995; Memorandum of Understanding (ceasefire) 22 February 2002; Eelam War IV 2006-2009.

wars.name: Operation Riviresa
wars.outcome: The army retook Jaffna, 'the key rebel stronghold'; the flag went up in Jaffna Fort on 5 December 1995.
wars.note: The page names the operation but gives no start date.

wars.name: Battle of Mullaitivu
wars.outcome: The LTTE 'decisively won the Battle of Mullaitivu on 18 July 1996' (Operation Unceasing Waves I).

wars.name: Battle of Elephant Pass (2000)
wars.outcome: The Elephant Pass complex 'fell into the hands of the LTTE' on 22 April 2000.

wars.name: Eastern Province campaign

zones.text: the Eastern Province: Batticaloa, Trincomalee and Ampara districts

wars.outcome: The army captured Thoppigala on 11 July 2007.

wars.name: Northern offensive (Vanni, 2008-2009)
wars.outcome: Mannar District lost by 2 August 2008, Kilinochchi taken 2 January 2009, Mullaitivu town 25 January 2009, the last pocket 18 May 2009.
wars.note: The civil-war page stops at December 2007 and does not cover this offensive; the LTTE and Tamil Eelam pages give the dates.

certainty.note: A de facto front: the Tigers held rural districts and the army held the towns; no treaty line before the ceasefire of 22 February 2002, and that left the line unsurveyed.

notes:
Written by sa-06-e on 2026-10-25 from the Sri Lankan civil war, Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam and Tamil Eelam pages. A rebel state Cliopatria lacks: the Tigers 'established and administered a de facto state under its control, named Tamil Eelam with Kilinochchi as its administrative capital' (LTTE page), with a civil police, courts, a bank and radio and television (Tamil Eelam page).
START. 1990 is a bridge (confidence 1): the pages give 'the 1990s-2000s' and the IPKF's departure of 1989-90, not a founding date; the LTTE itself dates from 5 May 1976. END. 18 May 2009, last pocket (Tamil Eelam page); the LTTE page dates Prabhakaran's death 19 May 2009 and its infobox ends the LTTE on 18 May.
EXTENT. All regions are whole Natural Earth districts, which overstate a front where the army held the towns. The pages give: Jaffna to 5 December 1995; Mullaitivu overrun 18 July 1996; Kilinochchi town taken 29 September 1996 and retaken 27 September 1998; the Vanni back in Tiger hands in 1999; Elephant Pass 22 April 2000; 76 percent of the Northern and Eastern provinces at the 2000 peak; the east lost 11 July 2007; Mannar District by 2 August 2008; Kilinochchi 2 January 2009; Mullaitivu town 25 January 2009. Vavuniya and Trincomalee town appear on no page. No area in km2 is given for the Tigers' holdings (the 18,880 km2 on the Tamil Eelam page is the claimed Tamil Eelam).
WIKIDATA. Not known to the researcher (unreachable); left null. Tamil Eelam's Wikipedia article is the page of the claimed state; a gap-filler may prefer 'Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam' for the identity page.
Mirror: every loss and gain here is the sri-lanka ledger's gain or loss against tamil-eelam.
